lines: A full review of the whole app, every finding fixed: your page reads right everywhere, and nothing is held back for ever by accident.
Interview records and the rules Claude learns from you are dated on your own day.
A chat doing one job for your page no longer republishes the page after an update.
A job started on an older copy waits for your word about updates where you chose that.
Employer job boards are read by openroles 0.5.1.
A chat saves your work without being woken when the save ends.
Conversations with no answer in about three months close by themselves. (set up for you)
A people search goes to the likely employers first.
A run's time is split into searching and reading.
Back from LinkedIn, the page shows you whose note you were sending.
Claude starts its LinkedIn work on your computer by itself.
Your computer's state, in one line.
To get your LinkedIn messages, invitations and own profile as files:
1. On LinkedIn, open Settings & Privacy, then Data privacy, then Get a copy of your data (some accounts call it Download your data).
2. Choose the larger download, the whole archive, and request it. LinkedIn may ask for your password.

3. LinkedIn emails you a link anything from about ten minutes to a day later, and it works for 72 hours. Attach the ZIP, or only the files you want me to read: messages.csv and Invitations.csv for your history; Profile.csv, Positions.csv, Education.csv, Skills.csv and Certifications.csv for your own profile.

tour.title: Brief
tour.text: Your day at a glance: what is booked, the next three things to do, who is waiting on you, the best new jobs, news that matters to your search and your numbers. Tap any line to go to it.

tour.title: To do
tour.text: What needs you, five at a time, most urgent first: a question, a follow-up that is due, an interview coming up. A card's filled button is its next step; the trash puts it away.

tour.title: Jobs
tour.text: Every role from found to applied. Found: scored out of 100 for how well it fits you; tap Draft this on one you like. Drafts: your resume and letter, checked; get the files, apply on the employer's site, tap I have applied. Applied: each one tracked, its follow-ups back in To do.

tour.title: Contacts
tour.text: Why people: someone inside who puts your name forward gets you far more interviews than applying cold. Claude finds who to write to and drafts a short note; you send it on LinkedIn yourself. Messages holds the notes ready to send. Tap a name to see everything about that person.

tour.title: Coming up
tour.text: Everything booked or due, by day: interviews, calls, tests and closing days. Add any of it to your calendar in a tap, and add anything else with Add something. Interviews shows each one's prep: what they will ask, your answers, your questions.

tour.title: Settings
tour.text: Your profile is the first thing here: your jobs, skills, education and certificates. Change them any time, and every new resume picks from them.

tour.title: Chat
tour.text: Ask anything, or paste a link, a message or a screenshot and say what you want. Claude does it, and the result shows up where it belongs.

every_hold.line: Jobs posted too long ago: your own window for how recent a job must be. Change How recent in Your rules.

Jobs that need a language, citizenship, clearance or qualification you do not have: the job's own words require it; looked at again whenever your profile changes. Tell Claude you have it, or add the language in Your rules.
Kinds of employer you will not work for: your choice, kept until you change it. Use the trash beside it in Your rules.
Employers you turned down: your choice, kept until you change it. Use the trash beside the employer in Your rules.

Jobs you set aside: 182 days after you set it aside, then it is shown once more; for good only where your own words said so (never, not at all, for good). Tap Bring back under Set aside in Jobs, or the bin beside it in Your rules.
Jobs a search already ruled out: a reason that was only a score, a pay band or a preference is read again on every search. Tap Bring back under What a search left out in Jobs.
A job Claude stopped drafting: 182 days after Claude stopped its draft, then it is shown once more. Tap Look again now under Held back for now.
The same job posted again: after 30 days the same title at the employer counts as a new opening. Add it yourself with Add a job.

Employers with no team for you where you look: on its own review day, or 90 days after it was found where it names none; an employer a people search found nobody who fits at is searched again after 30 days. Ask Claude to look at the employer again.

Other jobs at an employer you applied to: when they answer, or 45 days after you applied (or after the job's closing day) with no reply; a role scoring 10 points more still shows. Tell Claude to stop waiting on the employer.
Applying cold where someone is referring you: only you know when a referral is over; the job itself is never hidden. Tell Claude the referral there is over.
Follow-ups to an application: at most 2 follow-ups; closed as no reply after 45 days, and opened again if they write within 120 days. Say 'they replied' on the application.

More people at an employer where people are waiting on a reply: 2 people at a time; each one waiting frees their place about 9 days after the last message, once a follow-up is due by your rule; a connection request nobody accepted frees it after 21 days at most, and a conversation with no answer in 90 days is closed as gone cold. Ask Claude for more people at the employer.
Someone who has not answered your limit of messages: when they write back; your limit is 2 messages with no reply. Tap Close on their card, or paste their reply with They replied.
Conversations you closed or set aside: your choice; a reply from them opens it again. Ask Claude to write to them again.
People at employers you turned down: your choice, kept until you change the employer's rule. Use the trash beside the employer in Your rules.
People living outside where you look: your own places to look; a reply from them is always answered. Change Where in Your rules.
Someone you put on hold: on the day the hold names, or the day beside it. Ask Claude to write to them again.
Follow-ups to a request nobody accepted: when they accept, or when you withdraw it. Withdraw it from their card.
Someone already written to, offered as new: they are not someone new; what is owed them comes by your follow-up rule. Open their card in Contacts.
Paid LinkedIn messages, once this month's are used: on the first of next month. Tell Claude the number LinkedIn shows.
LinkedIn's weekly invitation limit: when LinkedIn lets requests go again; the app sets no limit of its own. Follow them meanwhile, and the request goes the next week.
Reading profiles after LinkedIn shows a check: the next day. Nothing to do.
A follow-up before its day: 6 weekdays after the last message. Draft it now on their card.
Something you put off: on the day you chose. Tap Show under put off in To do.
A first note you set aside: 182 days after you set it aside, then they are offered again; for good only where your own words said so (never). Tap Look again now under Held back for now, or Undo.
Chasing during interviews: a live process is never chased; after 14 quiet days Claude asks how it went. Say how it went, on the interview.
Prep and thank-you notes: prep shows 7 days before; a thank-you is offered for 7 days after. Tap Update my prep on the interview.
To do cards you hid: after a week, on that device. Tap Show under hidden this week in To do.
Ideas Claude suggests, after you dismiss three: 30 days after the third. Ask Claude to show you ideas again.
One idea you dismissed: your answer to that one idea. Tap Undo when it is said.
Your brief, paused: on the day you chose. Tap Resume in Settings, Your brief.
News a brief already carried: the same story twice is no news; at most 5 a brief. Choose how many in Settings, Your brief.
The LinkedIn download reminder, put off: it asks again on its next turn. Choose how often in Settings, LinkedIn.
Questions an update brought: they wait in Settings, never in To do, since nothing about them is late. Answer them under From updates in Settings.

rows.label: Look
rows.hint: Changes fonts, margins and where your name sits. Your words stay; one weak bullet may come off or go on to keep one page.

rows.label: Text size
rows.hint: Larger text is easier to read but fits one bullet fewer.

rows.label: Spacing
rows.hint: Roomier looks calmer and fits fewer bullets.

rows.label: Name and dates
rows.hint: Layout only.

rows.label: Colour
rows.hint: Only the colour of your name, headings and bullet marks. Every word stays where it is.

rows.label: Bullets
rows.hint: Swaps in another true bullet from your own history. Nothing is invented.

rows.label: Amount
rows.hint: Leaves white space instead of adding bullets. Never fewer than each job's minimum.

rows.label: Skills line
rows.hint: How many skills show. Only skills you hold; the posting's own words come first.

rows.label: Summary words
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Rewrites only the summary. It cannot add anything you haven't said.

rows.label: Length
rows.hint: Shorter letters get finished. The app keeps letters between 200 and 250 words.

rows.label: Tone
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Rewrites the opening, lead-in, bullets and closing in this tone. Facts do not change.

rows.label: Redo only
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Rewrites just that part and re-checks it.

rows.label: Addressed to
rows.hint: Only a name you or the posting gave.

rows.label: Length
rows.hint: Brief drops the opening line and the question; the plan's limit always holds.

rows.label: Formality
rows.hint: Contractions, greeting and exclamation marks only. Facts stay.

rows.label: Opening
rows.hint: How the note starts.

rows.label: The ask
rows.hint: How it ends. Asks for a chat, never the job.

rows.label: Order
rows.hint: Which sentence comes first.

rows.label: What to include
rows.hint: Recruiters need your work rights. The words are fixed so they stay true.

rows.label: Mention what you share
rows.hint: Names the school or employer you both have. Only one you both have.

rows.label: Another reason, or warmer
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Rewrites that part from what was read about them.

rows.label: Minimum score
rows.hint: Below 60 is a long shot.

rows.label: Work style
rows.hint: From the place text on each posting; not every posting says.

rows.label: How new
rows.hint: Old postings are often closed.

rows.label: Pay
rows.hint: Most postings omit pay; omitting it costs a role nothing.

rows.label: Search window
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Longer finds older, more often closed, postings.

rows.label: Where
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Adds places to search and keep.

rows.label: Job titles
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: A title must also pass the title filter, or it is searched and then dropped.

rows.label: Employers to watch
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Reads its own careers page.

rows.label: Job sites
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: A site that is off gets no request.

rows.label: How wide
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Wider reads more pages of each site.

rows.label: Pay floor
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: A stated range whose top is below this is flagged; below your cut line it is dropped.

rows.label: Stage and format
rows.hint: Which stage this is for, and its format: as assumed, and said so.

rows.label: How much
rows.hint: The one screen is what you read in the minutes before.

rows.label: Sections shown
rows.hint: Hiding changes what you see, not what is checked.

rows.label: Answer length
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: The time you will actually have. About 150 words a minute.

rows.label: Draft answers
rows.cost: Some Claude, about a minute or two
rows.hint: Marked Draft until you confirm. Written from your profile only.

rows.label: Length
rows.hint: How many owed items it lists.

rows.label: News items
rows.hint: Fewer is quicker to read.

rows.label: Stop watching
rows.hint: Tap any the brief should stop searching for. Claude will not add it back.

rows.label: Days and time
rows.hint: At most once a day.

rows.label: Parts shown
rows.hint: What is owed is always shown.

rows.label: Also watch
rows.hint: Something that moves your search, in your own words: a pay deal, a rule change, an employer. Searched in each brief, as often as you choose.

rows.label: How often
rows.hint: How often what you add is searched: as often as it really changes.

rows.label: Watch again
rows.hint: What you stopped watching, to bring back.
